title: Prime an insulin pen needle-up, then dial 24 units
instruction: Do the insulin pen's 2-unit flow check, then dial a 24-unit dose and hold the pen ready.
context: In hospitals and long-term care, nurses give insulin from pens on every medication round. Why: the maker's instructions for a FlexTouch pen require a flow check before each injection: turn the dose selector to 2 units, hold the pen with the needle pointing up, press and hold the dose button until the dose counter shows 0, and see a drop at the needle tip; then turn the selector to the prescribed dose. Held level or needle-down, the air in the cartridge stays in and the next dose is short. The hard part is physical: with parallel jaws the 15 cm pen must be turned upright in hand, held within 30 degrees of vertical while its 5.1 N button is held at its stop, and the bare needle kept off both jaws and every surface, then turned level to dial exactly 24. Done by: licensed practical nurses (O*NET 29-2061.00, "administer prescribed medications"; about 0.6 million in the US) and registered nurses on medication rounds, medical assistants in clinics, and the patients they teach.
setup: Table, robot behind it. A white moulded polystyrene (plastic) pen tray (200 x 60 x 12 mm, a 28 mm wide groove 4 mm deep along its length) lies 31 cm in front of the robot on its centre line, groove running front to back. In the groove: a Novo Nordisk Demonstration Pen for FlexTouch (the maker's training pen: a FlexTouch prefilled with 3 mL of liquid test medium, so a drop shows; 2-unit increments; the maker supplies it to healthcare professionals for training), pen cap off, a NovoFine 32G 6 mm needle screwed on and both needle caps removed (the maker's steps 1-6 done). The pen is about 24 mm across its ribbed barrel and 15 cm long without its cap, about 20 g; the needle points away from the robot, the dose selector (about 24 mm across, ribbed) and the dose button toward it; the dose window on top of the barrel, by the selector, shows 0. A 300 x 300 x 3 mm white silicone work mat lies to the left, its centre 30 cm in front of the robot and 19 cm left of the centre line. Starting layout fixed; the screenshot shows it.
scoring: Score 0 at any time, even if put right later, if the needle touches anything (tray, table, mat or either gripper; seen in the side or front video), the pen falls (rests anywhere but in a gripper or the tray groove), the dose button is pressed in to its stop with the counter above 2 units (a dose wasted), or the button is pressed a seventh time (presses counted in the video; the maker's limit is 6). A press is the flow check only if it takes the counter from 2 to 0 with the needle within 30 degrees of straight up from the start of the press until the counter shows 0 (side video: the needle end at least 13 cm higher than the button end throughout), and a drop shows at the needle tip after it (close-up photo). 0.25: the counter set to 2 with the pen lifted at least 2 cm off the tray. 0.5: a flow check done. 0.75: after it, the counter reads 24 units (dose pointer on the 24 mark in the window). 1.0: in addition, the pen (in the left gripper or back in the tray groove) is still (moves under 2 mm against a tape scale) for 2 s with the counter at 24 and the right gripper at least 3 cm from the pen. Anything else, including doing nothing, scores 0; the counter is re-read at the end.
reset_notes: Dial the pen back to 0 by turning the selector backwards (nothing is pushed out), wipe the needle tip and lay the pen back in the groove, needle away from the robot. Each trial uses 2 units of the 600-unit demonstration pen (about 250 trials); fit a new needle if one bends, put used needles in a sharps container, fit a silicone pad cover on each gripper finger, and keep people clear of the arms during a trial.
fidelity: Rigid pen, tray and mat; barrel and selector ribbed in section. Selector: a hinge clicking every 15 degrees, 2 units a click (declared). Button: a 2 mm slider at 5.1 N (maker's bench force); at its stop the torque spring pushes out 10 units/s (declared), turning the selector back; release stops it. The dose window shows the counter every step, numerals 14 mm tall (real: 4 mm). Liquid: 1 unit of air leaves first only with the needle up, then a drop shows. The needle has no collider.
